newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-TEARFUL OLAZABAL COMPLETES TRIUMPHANT RETURN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TEARFUL OLAZABAL COMPLETES TRIUMPHANT RETURN.

text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal completed a triumphant comeback to top competition on Sunday by winning the Turespana Masters, only the third tournament he has played after returning from a foot injury.

"At the 18th it was very special...many memories came to my mind, memories of the bad and hard times," said the 1994 U.S. Masters Champion who shot a six-under-par 67 to end the tournament two shots clear on a 20-below-par 272.
"It was very difficult to cope with, you know I never express my feelings and...you can see it is impossible not to do so now," said a tearful Olazabal.
"I didn't expect this win and I must still improve a lot for the Masters."
The Spaniard said he still suffered from the foot injury that had made walking difficult and had kept him out of the game for 18 months.
He also said that he would have to put in extra work with the driver.

Olazabal had started the day in third place, two shots behind joint leaders Lee Westwood of Britain -- who finished second -- and Argentine Jose Coceres, who dropped out of contention on a wind-affected final day with a one-over-par 74.
Eduardo Romero of Argentina and Briton Paul Broadhurst finished joint third, a further two shots behind Westwood.
